subject: Hospitality
title: Sharing Beds with Strangers
description: One-minute skill: Sharing Beds with Strangers.

hook.text: Until the 1800s, sharing a bed with a complete stranger at an inn was completely normal—even expected.

buildup.text: Rooms were rented by the bed, not by the room. Two or three strangers might share a single mattress.

discovery.text: Privacy was a luxury concept that didn't exist for most travelers. A bed was warmth and safety, not personal space.

twist.text: The private hotel room—one guest, one key—was a radical innovation of the early 1800s that we now take for granted.

climax.text: Tremont House in Boston (1829) was among the first to offer private rooms with locks. It was revolutionary.

punchline.text: Your private room is barely 200 years old. Privacy was invented.

quiz.question: What was revolutionary about the Tremont House in Boston (1829)?
options: It offered private rooms with locks—a new concept
